title: Umi
description: A Mac terminal for working with several coding agents.
body: Umi keeps agent sessions in tabs and panes. A sidebar lets you move between them while keeping the terminals where you left them.

title: Supervise agents in Warp
description: Start a session, wait for its reply and send a follow-up.
body: A command-line tool puts Claude Code and Codex in selected Warp panes. A script can follow a session through several turns while its terminal stays visible.

title: Use the coaching call for questions
description: An experiment in separating discovery from implementation.
body: “My plan is to use this call to just like ask you questions, figure out, and then shortly after the call, I'll send you kind of like an email with like some instructions and some ideas for us to try.”

title: Ask what changed after coaching
description: The evidence I want after a coaching session.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

I want to find ways for people to tell me what they actually did differently after we spoke.

title: What I want from an AI inbox
description: Two design choices I would explain alongside the prompt.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

I want the inbox to pick up new information without me reminding it that an email arrived. I also want to be able to skim the day’s tasks quickly.

title: Open the call with one question each
description: A format I tried for sharing AI-upskilling experience.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

I asked people to introduce themselves with a question. Then I left room for someone to pick one up, with the last five minutes set aside for everyone to write down their parting thoughts.

title: Map a recurring process
description: See where AI already helps and where there is room for more.
body: This single-file dashboard takes a process apart task by task. A prompt fills in the map, and the resulting HTML can travel with the assessment.

title: Ask a colleague’s AI a question
description: A prompt someone can run against their own work history.
body: The recipient’s assistant gathers the answer and prepares a report for its owner to review before sharing. The repository holds the common instructions that these prompts reference.

title: Short prompts leave room to explore
description: Why I sometimes give an agent only the goal.
body: “First, it's quicker to prompt if you just ask for the goal and then don't give the specifics so you can try more ideas.”

title: Make the tool easy to pass along
description: What I like about putting a working tool in a repository.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

Once a tool works, I want to be able to send a teammate one GitHub link. They can give it to their own coding agent and ask it to set the tool up.

title: Compare two versions of a skill’s output
description: Mark the passages you would keep, move, rewrite or remove.
body: A local review interface puts two outputs side by side. It saves judgments about individual passages and exports the decisions with the source versions.

title: What changes the shape of AI adoption?
description: An interactive notebook for exploring competing models of adoption.
body: Vary the reach of a tool, the rate at which tasks adopt it and the feedback between adopters. The curves illustrate the assumptions each model needs.

title: A one-page verdict for a tool trial
description: Record the question before running the trial.
body: A reusable trial structure puts the question, the tests and the verdict in one place. It gives the next experiment a previous decision to build on.

title: How much time would you invest in fixing this?
description: A question I use to decide whether a workflow is worth improving.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

Before proposing an automation, I ask how much time the person was already planning to spend improving that process over the next few weeks. It gives us a starting point for discussing the payoff.

title: Inside an agent’s desk
description: A worked example of a filing system for ongoing agent work.
body: The example includes Markdown filing conventions, a morning docket and the prompts that turn incoming material into drafts. Its sample records are fictional.

title: Find the first task to automate
description: Turn a week of recurring work into a ranked shortlist.
body: The prompts go from identifying repeated tasks to writing a structured entry for each one. The final step sketches a first implementation of the most promising task.

title: Give the end-of-day reflection some evidence
description: A possible use for an agent when I cannot remember what filled the day.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

When I sit down to reflect, I often have to reconstruct what I actually did first. I wondered whether an agent could gather that record so I could spend the time deciding what mattered.

title: Read an AI-generated sharing report
description: Package a report as one HTML file.
body: A prompt inserts structured findings into a standalone viewer. The reader can open the filled-in file directly.

title: Leave real suggested edits from Claude
description: Google Docs comments, replies and suggested edits through an MCP server.
body: The implementation exposes document review operations to an assistant. It provides a concrete counterpart to the tests of what existing Docs connectors can do.

title: Refresh a published article
description: Find claims whose evidence or links have changed.
body: The pipeline looks for a source that warrants a specific update and places the proposed edit into a Google Doc for review.

title: Murmur
description: Dictate a prompt directly into the text field you are using.
body: This Mac app transcribes speech on the device. A keyboard shortcut starts dictation and returns the text to the cursor.

title: Designing an introduction to delegation
description: Draft lessons and discarded approaches to introducing Claude.
body: The repository records attempts to teach delegation through practice. The writing and lesson structure are still being revised.

title: Comment in the margin of a web page
description: Select a passage on a page and start a discussion beside it.
body: The browser extension anchors a thread to the selected text. The discussion stays attached to the passage as people add replies.

title: Give people a place to practise
description: An experiment I wanted to try with a recurring workshop.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

I wanted to try a weekly or fortnightly session where people could bring real work and spend a few hours trying Claude Code, with someone nearby when they got stuck.

title: Test a Google Docs connector
description: A test harness for ordinary editing requests on a synthetic project plan.
body: The repository pairs connector gaps with a methodology and sample runs. Checking the resulting document makes it possible to distinguish a completed edit from an assistant saying it made one.

title: Run one repetition all the way through
description: What I would hand over before scaling a recurring workflow.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

I would first run the automation myself, all the way to an output I could use. That gives someone else a worked example to take over, especially when the same task needs doing a hundred times.

title: Ask an agent to tour a product
description: A way to find out what a tool can actually do.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

I sometimes want an agent to read the documentation and then use the interface. I would like it to tell me which features it actually found when it clicked around.

title: Solve something together on the first call
description: My original test for a coaching session.
body:
Paraphrased from a call.

I started by asking how the person already used AI and where they got stuck. I wanted to solve something together on the call that would make them excited to try more on their own.
